latest_release.body:
# 4.46.0

## Features

- **Run web apps in `serverless dev`.** `serverless dev` now runs a service's web apps on your machine, in the same session as its functions and with no redeploy. Requests to the web app's real URL (and a custom domain in front of it) reach your local server, which gets the deployed environment variables and the web app's execution-role credentials. A local URL on `localhost` serves it with your framework's hot reload. Set `webApps.<name>.dev.command` to start a dev server such as `next dev`, or leave it out to run `entry` from source. When your machine doesn't answer in time, the deployed code answers instead, and stopping the session puts the deployed code back. `--web-app` and `--skip-web-app` choose which web apps run, and `--local-only` keeps the real URL on the deployed code. Requests are recorded for `serverless dev requests` and `serverless dev replay`, as invocations are. Read more in the [Dev Mode guide](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/dev-mode#web-apps) and the [`serverless dev` reference](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/cli-reference/dev), and try the [Next.js example](https://github.com/serverless/examples/tree/v4/aws-node-nextjs-web-app). (#14059)

```yaml
webApps:
  site:
    entry: .next/standalone/server.js
    dev:
      command: next dev --hostname 127.0.0.1 # run with PORT and HOSTNAME set
```

```bash
serverless dev --stage alice --web-app site
```

- **Subscribe functions to EventBridge Custom Event Buses.** When `eventBus` is a Custom Event Bus (its ARN, a variable that resolves to one, or a `Ref` or `Fn::GetAtt … EventBusArn` to an `AWS::EventsV2::EventBus` in `resources`), the `eventBridge` event subscribes the function to it. Functions receive arrays of up to 10 events per call, with AWS's retry policy. New settings switch each default: `ordering: fifo` for ordered delivery, `batchSize`, `maximumBatchingWindow`, `async`, `resumePosition` and `role`. The Framework creates one delivery role per service. Bus names, the default bus and Classic event bus ARNs work as before. `serverless agent inspect` shows the subscribers and buses. Read more in [Custom Event Bus](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/events/event-bridge#custom-event-bus), and try the [Compose example](https://github.com/serverless/examples/tree/v4/compose-eventbridge-custom-bus). (#14051)

```yaml
functions:
  processOrder:
    handler: handler.process
    events:
      - eventBridge:
          eventBus: !GetAtt OrdersBus.EventBusArn
          ordering: fifo
          pattern:
            source:
              - orders.service

resources:
  Resources:
    OrdersBus:
      Type: AWS::EventsV2::EventBus
      Properties:
        Name: orders
```

- **`serverless invoke` reaches durable functions.** Without `--qualifier`, `serverless invoke` now targets the alias a durable function's deploy publishes. The durable execution ARN is printed (`Durable execution started: <arn>` with `--type Event`), and the new `--json` flag prints one object with the status code, qualifier, executed version, durable execution ARN, function error, payload and log. A synchronous invoke of a function whose `executionTimeout` is above 900 seconds stops before calling Lambda and suggests `--type Event`. `durableConfig` now also applies to OS-only runtimes from `provided.al2023` (for example Go) and to container image functions. Read more in [Durable Functions](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/functions#durable-functions) and [invoking durable functions](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/cli-reference/invoke#durable-functions). (#14049)

```bash
serverless invoke -f checkout --type Event --durable-execution-name order-1042 --json
```

**The Serverless Framework** – Makes it easy to use AWS Lambda and other managed cloud services to build applications that auto-scale, cost nothing when idle, and result in radically low maintenance. The Serverless Framework is a command-line tool with approachable YAML syntax to deploy both your code and cloud infrastructure needed to make tons of serverless application use-cases, like APIs, front-ends, data pipelines and scheduled tasks. It's a multi-language framework that supports Node.js, Typescript, Python, Go, Java, and more. It's also completely extensible via over 1,000 plugins which add more serverless use-cases and workflows to the Framework. Actively maintained by [Serverless Inc](https://www.serverless.com).
# Serverless Framework - V.4

**October 2026** – V.4 continues to feature significant updates. Review them all below. Recent releases added Web Apps on AWS Lambda Web Functions, MCP server hosting on AWS Lambda, a rebuilt Dev Mode, built-in support for AI coding agents, Sandboxes (isolated, ephemeral compute on AWS Lambda), native Amazon Bedrock AgentCore support, Managed Instances, Durable Functions, and built-in AWS Login & SSO. As always, we are more excited about the serverless future than ever. ## New Features In V.4 Here's a list of everything that's new in V.4, so far: - **Web Apps** – Run Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js and other Node.js HTTP servers on AWS Lambda Web Functions. Define a server under the top-level `webApps` block and `serverless deploy` packages it, creates the web function and its HTTPS endpoint, and prints the URL. Your code listens on `process.env.PORT` as it does locally — no handler to export and no adapter to install. Custom domains are served through Amazon CloudFront. [More info here](https://www.serverless.com/framework/docs/providers/aws/guide/web-apps). -
